source_review.notes: Checked the current CNCF Platforms White Paper and Platform Engineering Maturity Model, the DORA platform-engineering capability page updated in 2026, DORA's corrected 2024 report record, the original Bottcher and Kennedy practitioner essays, the ACM SPACE paper, and Google's SRE toil chapter. Current and empirical claims are qualified by source date, method, context, and non-causal limits.

evidence: Checked journey J, consuming teams U, platform team P, providers Q, capability contract K, before burden C_b, residual burden C_u, platform burden C_p, coordination burden C_c, team count n, benefit B and value delta notation.
Checked that each complexity category and responsibility mode is defined before operational use.
Checked the value expression's parentheses and signs against the stated before-versus-after accounting interpretation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Burden and benefit are explicitly vectors; the expression is not presented as a naturally measurable universal scalar.

evidence: Confirmed illustrative handoffs 5+4+4 equal baseline 13.
Confirmed remaining handoffs 1+1+1 equal 3 and difference equals 10.
Confirmed four platform-owned capability labels and six residual team-decision labels.
Confirmed all six stdout lines exactly match the snippet annotation and generated report.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The handoff counts are illustrative inputs, not measured productivity or lead-time results.

evidence: Expanded the total-system accounting as avoided per-team burden nC_b minus platform, coordination and residual per-team burdens plus benefit B.
Checked that a lower consumer-interface burden alone cannot imply positive total value because C_p and C_c may dominate.
Checked that different cost bearers and vector dimensions prevent unqualified aggregation.
Traced own, enable, verify and observe responsibility modes against authority and capability boundaries.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The value frame organizes evidence and trade-offs; it does not prove causal platform return.

evidence: Reviewed no platform, documentation, standard, library, template, managed service, shared service, federated platform and custom control-plane alternatives.
Reviewed ordinary, novice, expert, unusual workload, accessibility, regulatory, escape-hatch, provider-failure and retirement paths.
Reviewed manual queues behind portals, opaque failures, quota exhaustion, invalid standardization, low adoption, mandated adoption, shadow alternatives and concentrated platform outages.

Reviewed clinical model deployment and public-benefits eligibility with domain, legal, clinical/civil-rights, accessibility, privacy, security, reliability, regulatory, affected-user and independent assurance roles.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Clinical and public-benefits authorization remain human and institutional decisions outside repository validation.

evidence: Checked observed user work drives scope rather than tool inventory.
Checked domain semantics, authorization, data meaning, service objectives and risk acceptance remain with accountable authorities.
Checked every platform interface requires operating ownership, diagnostics, lifecycle, support and retirement.
Checked routine valid requests avoid hidden manual fulfillment while exceptions remain explicit and bounded.
Checked default paths encode reviewed security and reliability without converting a recommendation into universal fit.
Checked total-effects measurement includes platform-team cost, migration, excluded users, escape, and central blast radius.
invariant_checking.notes: Capability-specific invariants still require implementation, operational, security and user evidence.

evidence: Reviewed counterexample in which a portal merely fronts a manual ticket queue and therefore does not establish self-service.
Reviewed complexity-transfer argument showing a simple consumer API can increase central control-plane, security, support and migration burden.
Reviewed the adoption counterexample showing mandates and absent alternatives can produce use without product value.
Reviewed domain-authority counterexamples for application authorization, clinical models and benefits eligibility.
Confirmed executable arithmetic and research associations are not presented as proof of causality, productivity or organizational fit.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies accounting arguments and falsifying cases, not a formal theorem of platform success.

evidence: Audited uses of eliminates, reduces, improves, value, productivity, self-service, safe, reliable, proof, maturity and success.
All outcome claims require observed journeys and multiple evidence dimensions; empirical findings retain source and qualification.
The executable limitation rejects causal, productivity, cognitive-load, reliability, security, economic, fit and boundary-correctness claims.
No external academic, practitioner, clinical, legal, regulatory, public-sector or affected-community review is claimed.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: High-consequence platform acceptance remains explicitly assigned to named human and institutional reviewers.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/PLAT-001/report.json

Reproduced three encoded journeys, 13 baseline handoffs, three residual handoffs, ten removed handoffs, four platform-owned capability labels and six residual team decisions under the recorded Python 3 toolchain.
Confirmed exact expected stdout and empty stderr.
Confirmed execution uses no network, dependencies, filesystem mutation or external state.
Confirmed the chapter treats counts as arithmetic illustration rather than field evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes only the deterministic accounting example.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter defines platform engineering through total-system complexity, user outcomes, sociotechnical ownership and product responsibility while reserving later modules' detailed ownership of consumers, cognitive load, product practice, self-service, paved roads, capabilities, platforms versus clouds, team boundaries and value propositions.

practitioner_review.notes: Production guidance covers journey observation, capability selection, responsibility maps, thinnest viable layers, lifecycle self-service, guardrails, diagnostics, support, platform reliability, escape, provider use, adoption, balanced measures, migration and retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with ten examples and five exercises progressing from tools versus capabilities and ticket queues through ownership, telemetry, abstraction failures, workload diversity, measurement, providers, high-stakes domain authority and retirement.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
